Eli (Design): Quick flag 8: in request drilldown header the Copy ID icon is after Close. Keyboard flow goes Export -> Close -> Copy which feels out of order. Thoughts? Priya (Product): We surfaced Copy to be super quick for support, but agree order shouldn't be jarring. Do we have analytics on Copy vs Export frequency? Zoe (Eng-UX): Copy is frequent but not as frequent as Export in some orgs. Suggestion: keep Export primary, but place Copy immediately adjacent to Close so the tab order is Export -> Close -> Copy. On small screens collapse Copy into kebab. Noah (Eng-Frontend): Implementation note: current markup has `tabindex="-1"` on the icon which breaks focus. I'll remove that and ensure DOM order matches visual order. Also add `aria-label` to icon-only controls. Samir (Accessibility): Please use explicit `aria-label="Copy correlation ID"`. Announce copy action with a live region: `
Correlation ID copied.
`. Don't read the full ID aloud. Also ensure export button color meets 4.5:1 contrast. Eli (Design): Microcopy: prefer "Download bundle" for primary and "Export JSON" in menu. Add tiny helper: "Bundle includes spans, logs, and attachments." Keeps things clear. Priya (Product): Agree. Also keep analytics stable: event `trace_export.clicked` plus property `variant=bundle|json`. For copy use `trace_copy.clicked` with `target=correlation_id`. Noah (Eng-Frontend): I'll file a small PR: 1) reorder DOM so Copy sits next to Close on desktop 2) collapse to kebab on mobile 3) add `aria-label`s and live region 4) tweak CSS for contrast. Will include contrast screenshots and a 8s keyboard video in PR. Samir (Accessibility): Checklist for review: aria-labels, role=status live region, no tooltip-only labeling, menu uses ARIA menu patterns, color contrast evidence, keyboard demo. deploy-bot: Heads up: Low-risk UI deploy window tomorrow 00:30-01:30 UTC. Priya (Product): Thanks all 93. If Noah's PR is small we'll ship it in next minor. After deploy we'll run a quick internal a11y check and 2-person hallway test. Ping me for blockers.
